title: Case 1: Canonical Splice Site Destruction (Likely Pathogenic)

patient_context.indication: Maternal history of early-onset breast cancer (age 42) and personal history of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) at age 38. Comprehensive hereditary cancer multigene sequencing reported a BRCA1 VUS.

biological_details.clinical_impact_summary: Obliterates canonical splice donor consensus 'GT', causing complete failure of intron excision and premature termination.

literature_references.citation: SpliceVarDB Consortium. (2024). SpliceVarDB: A comprehensive database of experimentally validated human splicing variants.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: Minigene and patient RNA-seq assays demonstrate complete abolition of normal donor splicing, leading to exon skipping and frameshift.

literature_references.citation: Findlay, G. M., et al. (2018). Accurate classification of BRCA1 variants with saturation genome editing.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 reveals that invariant +1 donor substitutions cause complete loss of cellular fitness, functioning as null alleles.

literature_references.citation: Avsec, Ž., et al. (2026). Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: AlphaGenome accurately predicts donor collapse (delta 0.9957) utilizing 1 Mb sequence context, achieving 0.993 ROC AUC on intronic variants.

title: Case 2: Exonic Silent Variant near Splice Junction (Likely Benign)

patient_context.indication: Strong family history of ovarian cancer (paternal aunt and grandmother). Patient sought preventive genetic testing; sequencing flagged an exonic BRCA1 VUS.

biological_details.exon_context: Exon 10 (historically Exon 11), large internal coding exon
biological_details.clinical_impact_summary: Does not disrupt splice donor/acceptor machinery or create de novo cryptic splice signals; splicing kinetics remain intact.

literature_references.citation: SpliceVarDB Consortium. (2024). SpliceVarDB: A comprehensive database of experimentally validated human splicing variants.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: High-throughput functional splicing screen confirms normal transcript ratios with zero evidence of aberrant splicing or exon exclusion.

literature_references.citation: Davy, G., et al. (2017). Assessment of splicing alterations for BRCA1/2 exonic variants.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: Comprehensive minigene evaluation demonstrates that exonic alterations in central Exon 10 lack exonic splicing enhancer (ESE) disruptive effects.

literature_references.citation: Avsec, Ž., et al. (2026). Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: AlphaGenome scores this variant in Bin 1 (Score 0.016), reflecting <1.5% empirical risk of splicing disruption across 734 RNA-seq tissue tracks.

title: Case 3: Deep-Intronic Cryptic Splice Activation (Priority Candidate)

patient_context.indication: Bilateral breast cancer in two first-degree relatives. Standard exome testing was negative; whole-genome sequencing identified a deep-intronic variant of uncertain significance.

biological_details.exon_context: Intron 10 (4,105 base pairs downstream of Exon 10 donor site)
biological_details.clinical_impact_summary: Activates a de novo pseudoexon / cryptic splice site 4,105 bp deep inside the intron. Undetectable by standard proximity heuristics (1/distance = 0.00024), but captured by AlphaGenome's 100 kb context window.

literature_references.citation: SpliceVarDB Consortium. (2024). SpliceVarDB: A comprehensive database of experimentally validated human splicing variants.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: SpliceVarDB catalogues this deep-intronic substitution as an active splice-altering variant identified via targeted transcript sequencing.

literature_references.citation: Fraile-Bethencourt, E., et al. (2019). De novo cryptic splice site activation in deep intronic regions of cancer predisposition genes.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: Deep intronic SNVs in BRCA1 can generate high-affinity 5' donor motifs that incorporate out-of-frame pseudoexons, causing loss of tumor suppressor function.

literature_references.citation: Avsec, Ž., et al. (2026). Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome.
literature_references.clinical_takeaway: AlphaGenome's long context window flags this variant with high delta (0.652 site delta), outperforming standard distance tools (ROC AUC 0.993 vs. 0.914).
